title: The coordinate map has a kernel fork which is a limit, by the two-chart locally split calculation.
statement: Let k be a field, P=Proj k[x_0,x_1] with the standard grading [def-sc-p1-standard], G any O_P-module, and z an integer. With twists and coordinate multiplication as in [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf], there exists f:G(z-1) -> G(z) ⊕ G(z) whose composite with (μ_0(z),μ_1(z)) is zero and whose resulting kernel fork is a limit.

source.place: Two-chart calculation, proof steps 1 and 2 (not an application of the parent theorem)

proof.text: Construct the map f as the binary biproduct lift of minus coordinate 1 and coordinate 0 at degree z-1, with the equality transport (z-1)+1=z. Proj.twistMul_comp_twistMul, whiskering, and biprod.lift_desc prove its composite with the quotient is zero.

Prove the elementary categorical local kernel criterion: when the quotient is p;c+q;d, the maps p and q are jointly monic, f;g=0, and f;q and c are invertible, a killed arrow b factors as b;q;inv(f;q). Equality of q components and vanishing under g imply equality of p components by cancellation of c. Invertibility of f;q also gives uniqueness. Apply this criterion to either ordering of the biproduct projections.

On the chart D+(x_i), Proj.isIso_restrict_twistMul and the monoidal pullback comparison make both adjacent coordinate multiplication maps invertible after tensoring with G. The local criterion therefore proves the mapped explicit fork is a limit on each chart. Restriction preserves limits by Scheme.Modules.preservesLimitsOfSize_restrictFunctor.

Choose an existing abstract limit cone for the quotient and lift the explicit fork into it. Each restricted lift is an isomorphism by comparison of two limit cones. The coordinate basic opens cover Proj by the irrelevant-ideal computation. Scheme.Modules.bijective_stalk_of_isIso_restrict and the sheaf stalk criterion make the global comparison an isomorphism. The IsLimit.nonempty_isLimit_iff_isIso_lift criterion gives the required global limiting fork. The selected cone is determined up to unique isomorphism by its proved universal property; f itself is an explicit construction.

proof_origin.place: Original two-chart locally split calculation, implemented in Lean by T2; categorical universal-property and stalkwise gluing arguments

lean.statement:
theorem exists_proj_coordinate_kernel_fork
    (k : Type u) [Field k]
    (G : (Proj (MvPolynomial.homogeneousSubmodule (Fin 2) k)).Modules) (z : ℤ) :
    ∃ (f : G ⊗ Proj.twist (MvPolynomial.homogeneousSubmodule (Fin 2) k) (z - 1) ⟶
        (G ⊗ Proj.twist (MvPolynomial.homogeneousSubmodule (Fin 2) k) z) ⊞
        (G ⊗ Proj.twist (MvPolynomial.homogeneousSubmodule (Fin 2) k) z))
      (h : f ≫ biprod.desc
        (G ◁ Proj.twistMul z (MvPolynomial.X_mem_homogeneousSubmodule_one k (0 : Fin 2)))
        (G ◁ Proj.twistMul z (MvPolynomial.X_mem_homogeneousSubmodule_one k (1 : Fin 2))) = 0),
      Nonempty (IsLimit (KernelFork.ofι f h))
